newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Optimism grows France to drop opposition to Annan.
newsitem.headline: Optimism grows France to drop opposition to Annan.

text.p: Diplomats expressed growing optimism on Friday that France would drop its opposition to the nomination of Kofi Annan of Ghana to be the next U.N. secretary-general.

Several members of the Security Council and senior U.N. officials, speaking off the record, said they were fairly sure an unofficial poll scheduled for later in the day would give Annan the votes of all 15 council members.
Annan, the U.N. Undersecretary-General for peacekeeping operations, obtained 14 votes in the most recent unofficial poll on Thursday, with France the only holdout.
The five permanent council members -- the United States, Russia, Britain, China and France -- have the power of veto in any formal voting.

Annan's 14-1 showing -- his best in seven unofficial polls so far -- equalled the vote obtained by incumbent Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali in a formal council vote Nov. 19 in which the Egyptian diplomat, the only candidate, was vetoed by the United States. Washington says the United Nations needs new leadership to introduce reforms.
Boutros-Ghali later suspended his candidacy and four other African hopefuls entered the race, including Annan, who led consistently on each of the unofficial ballots.
